Adam Bauman

Republican candidate for U.S. Representative, District 16, El Paso County, Texas · Challenger

Retired U.S. Border Patrol agent; owner of a canine narcotics detection business (Bauman Tactical Canine)

Adam Bauman is a U.S. Navy veteran and retired U.S. Border Patrol agent who came to El Paso in 2001 when Border Patrol stationed him there, and he now runs a canine drug detection business. This is his first run for public office. He was one of seven candidates in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary and won the May 26, 2026 runoff against Manuel Barraza with 69% of the vote, so he faces Democratic incumbent Veronica Escobar on November 3.

Where Bauman stands

Property taxes
Lists lowering property taxes as a priority. Says El Paso's property taxes are among the highest in Texas, blames school budgets and PR bonds (cashless bail), and pledges to work with local leaders to make them more affordable.
Federal funding to local governments
Agrees property taxes are set by local governments, not Congress. Says he would make sure federal money sent to local entities is "appropriated correctly."
Immigration enforcement
Says legal immigration is needed. Argues current deportation efforts are "enforcing the laws that are on the books" and says ICE agents should be commended for doing their jobs.
Detention conditions
Responding to unrest at Camp East Montana, said the effort to check conditions there should also go to the El Paso County Detention Facility, so that people held there are treated appropriately.
Congressional term limits
Supports limiting members of Congress to three terms.

Background

  • U.S. Navy veteran
  • U.S. Customs and Border Protection: Border Patrol agent, including the Border Patrol Tactical Unit (stationed in El Paso from 2001); retired
  • Owner of Bauman Tactical Canine (canine narcotics detection), operating since 2020 per county records
  • Host of the podcast "The Adam Bauman Show"
  • Born in Phoenix, Arizona
  • No prior elected office; 2026 is his first run
  • Won the 2026 Republican nomination for TX-16 in the May 26 runoff (69%)
  • Education: not found in sources reviewed
